title: USP39 promotes antiviral defense through post-transcriptional control of RIG-I and stabilization of STING
experiments_summary:
1. **RNA virus infection in macrophages**: Usp39fl/fl Lyz2Cre (USP39-deficient) and control macrophages were infected with VSV or H1N1 PR8; viral replication was measured by qPCR (VSV-N and H1N1 PR8 mRNA), flow cytometry (VSV-eGFP), and TCID50 assay of supernatants. Type I IFN responses (Ifn-β, Ifn-α4 mRNA by qPCR; IFN-β protein by ELISA) and ISG expression (Isg15, Isg56, Cxcl10) were also assessed. Poly(I:C) transfection was used as an RIG-I agonist in the same cell system.

2. **USP39 overexpression in HeLa/HEK293T cells**: HA-USP39 plasmid was overexpressed in HeLa cells followed by VSV or H1N1 PR8 infection; viral replication and Ifn-β mRNA were measured by qPCR and fluorescence microscopy.

3. **DNA virus infection in macrophages**: USP39-deficient and control macrophages were infected with HSV-1 or HSV-2; viral mRNA (UL30, ICP27), Ifn-β/Ifn-α4 mRNA, IFN-β protein, and ISG mRNAs were measured. dsDNA transfection was used as a cGAS-STING pathway activator. USP39 overexpression in HeLa cells was tested similarly with HSV-1/HSV-2.

4. **In vivo viral infection**: Usp39fl/fl Lyz2Cre and control mice (8–12 weeks) were infected with VSV (tail vein) or HSV-1 (tail vein or intraperitoneal injection). Ifn-β and Ifn-α4 mRNA in spleen, liver, and lung (qPCR), serum IFN-β (ELISA), viral titers in organs (TCID50), survival curves (Kaplan–Meier), and lung histology (H&E staining) were assessed.

5. **Signaling pathway analysis by western blotting**: Protein levels of RIG-I, MAVS, STING, p-TBK1, and TBK1 were examined by western blot in USP39-deficient macrophages and USP39-overexpressing HEK293T cells after VSV, Poly(I:C), HSV-1, dsDNA, or cGAMP stimulation. Flag-RIG-I, Flag-STING, and Flag-TBK1 were overexpressed with or without Myc-USP39 to identify specific targets.

6. **Ubiquitination assay for RIG-I**: Myc-USP39 and Flag-RIG-I were co-transfected in HEK293T cells with MG132 treatment; immunoprecipitation followed by western blot was used to assess RIG-I ubiquitination levels.

7. **Rig-i pre-mRNA splicing analysis**: Usp39 siRNA knockdown in macrophages, Usp39fl/fl Lyz2Cre macrophages, and HA-USP39 overexpressing HeLa cells were analyzed by qPCR using primers spanning exon-exon (spliced) and exon-intron (unspliced) junctions of mouse and human Rig-i. Spliced-to-unspliced ratios across all 18 exon-intron junctions of mouse Rig-i were examined in BMDMs. The same analyses were repeated after Poly(I:C) transfection and VSV infection.

8. **RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) assay**: HA-USP39 was overexpressed in HEK293T cells; RIP was performed using a Magna RIP kit, and co-precipitated RIG-I pre-mRNA and mature mRNA were detected by PCR and qPCR.

9. **USP39 rescue experiments**: USP39 was restored in Usp39fl/fl Lyz2Cre BMDMs via lentiviral transduction; Ifn-β mRNA, VSV replication, Rig-i mRNA levels, and exon-to-intron splicing ratios were re-assessed. USP39-CA (C306A enzyme-inactive mutant) was compared to wild-type USP39 for effects on Rig-i mRNA and splicing in HeLa cells infected with VSV.

10. **STAT1-knockout control experiments**: USP39-promoted Ifn-β expression and Rig-i pre-mRNA splicing were assessed in STAT1-knockout cells to rule out indirect effects via IFN-IFNAR-JAK/STAT signaling.

11. **USP39–STING interaction studies**: STING mRNA levels in USP39-deficient macrophages were measured by qPCR. Co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) with Flag- or His-STING and Myc-USP39 overexpressed in HEK293T cells, immunofluorescence co-localization, and GST pulldown assay (using bacterially expressed GST-USP39 and HEK293T-expressed Flag-STING) were performed to confirm direct interaction.

12. **STING stability and degradation assays**: Cycloheximide chase assay in HEK293T cells with or without USP39 overexpression assessed STING protein stability. MG132 treatment of Usp39fl/fl Lyz2Cre macrophages tested proteasomal degradation dependency.

13. **STING ubiquitination assays**: HA-Ub-WT or HA-Ub-K48 constructs were co-transfected with Flag-STING and Myc-USP39 (or Myc-USP39-CA) in HEK293T cells; immunoprecipitation followed by western blot quantified K48-linked polyubiquitination of STING. K48-linked STING ubiquitination was also compared between Usp39fl/fl Lyz2Cre and control macrophages. An OTUB1 co-expression assay was used to verify covalent ubiquitin chain conjugation to STING.

14. **Identification of USP39 deubiquitination site on STING**: Four conserved lysine residues of STING (K235, K288, K369, K377) identified via UniProt were individually mutated to arginine; each mutant was co-transfected with Myc-USP39 in HEK293T cells and K48-linked ubiquitination assessed by co-IP/western blot to identify the specific site (K288) targeted by USP39.

15. **HSV-1 rescue experiments in USP39-deficient BMDMs**: USP39 was restored in Usp39fl/fl Lyz2Cre BMDMs by lentiviral transduction; Ifn-β mRNA and HSV-1 replication were measured after HSV-1 infection. Wild-type USP39 versus USP39-CA effects on STING protein levels and K48-linked STING ubiquitination were compared in HEK293T cells.
